title: The unusual cluster Terzan 5
caption: The star cluster Terzan 5, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This Hubble image shows Terzan 5, a stellar cluster hidden in the bulge, the dense, dusty crowd of stars around the centre of the Milky Way. Thick dust clouds lie between us and the cluster, so seeing its stars clearly means peering through that veil.
An international team of astronomers did just that and found an unusual mix of stars in the cluster. Their observations showed that the stars in Terzan 5 are a surprisingly varied population.

The results suggest that Terzan 5 is really one of the bulge's primordial building blocks. It is most likely a relic from the very early days of the Milky Way, a surviving fragment of the material from which the central part of our galaxy was assembled.

understand.summary: The image combines visible and near-infrared data from Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys and near-infrared data from Wide Field Camera 3. The source does not publish which colour was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: Infrared light is invisible to the eye, and it passes through dust more easily than visible light, which helps reveal stars behind the bulge's thick dust clouds.
